policy.headline: Small, steady updates: five Minor updates, then the next Major. Serious fixes still ship the moment they're tested.
points: This page updates itself. When a release is published, edited or removed on GitHub, it moves from Coming up to Recently released within a couple of minutes.
Updates come in cycles. A Major update (like 1.5) starts a cycle. It is followed by five Minor updates, and then the next Major (1.6).
A Minor update is small and has one theme. The fifth Minor of every cycle is a Stability update: no new features, just fixes, speed, safety checks and tidying up.
A Hotfix is an urgent fix for something serious, like anything that could lose your data. It doesn't wait its turn and it doesn't count toward the five.

Every update carries a tag shown beside its version number: MAJOR, MINOR, STABILITY or HOTFIX. An update can also carry a BETA tag while it is being tried out. A beta is published as a pre-release that the automatic updater skips, so only people who choose to download it get it. A tag is a separate label, so the version number never changes, and when a beta is ready the BETA tag simply comes off. Betas apply to the downloads (desktop installers and the browser zip); the website only ever shows a finished version.

A single feature can carry a BETA tag too, shown beside it in the list. It still comes in a finished update that everyone gets, but it is newer and less proven, so it may change, or be switched off if it causes trouble. When it has proved itself the tag comes off.
Version numbers only go up, so a Hotfix in the middle of a cycle moves the numbers after it up by one. The tags always say what each update is.

Each update has a desktop number and a browser number that move together (desktop 1.4.1 comes with browser 3.0.1). Dates are set when an update is nearly ready. If one isn't ready or hasn't been tested properly, it moves instead of shipping, and this page says so.
The browser version (the website) updates as soon as the new version is put online, and shows a bar when a newer version is ready. The browser zip is attached to every release.

Windows and Linux can update by themselves (version 1.3.2 and newer). In Control Panel you choose: install automatically, ask me first, or just tell me. On a Mac the app tells you when an update is out and links to the download, because Apple's signing isn't paid for yet.
Windows is tested on a real PC. Linux can only be tested in a virtual environment.
notified: Press Watch on the GitHub page, then Custom, then Releases, to get an email for each release.
Add the releases feed to your feed reader.
In the desktop app, Control Panel shows when it last checked for updates and what it found.

upcoming.title: Fixes and polish
items: A new logo on the Start button

items.text: Clipy can edit and complete things you already have (it asks first, and Undo puts it back)

items: The Settings items in the Start menu jump straight to the right part of Control Panel
Browser: the storage bar shows what is using the space, and its numbers are double-checked
Browser: a clearer way to pick your backup folder, with help for Chrome's "contains system files" message

items.text: Browser: choose the backup file instead of a folder

items: Desktop: a new Mac menu bar icon

items.text: Desktop: a red number on the Mac Dock icon (optional)

items: Desktop: Ask Clipy and Mini timer in the Windows taskbar menu

items.text: Desktop: pop-outs remember their size, place and screen more reliably

items: Support for Update & feature based tags (a small label like BETA beside an update or a single feature)
upcoming.note: Date to be set. Features marked BETA are newer and less proven. Anything that can't be tested properly moves to a later Minor update.

upcoming.title: Safety net
items: Undo for deleting things, and a heads-up about duplicates
Updates can have more than one tag (for example a Major that was released again with a fix is MAJOR and HOTFIX)
Browser: the storage numbers now add up (daily snapshots are counted as copies), and the empty space under the storage bar is gone
Desktop: the empty space under the storage section is gone
Features that were BETA in 1.4.1 are now final (the pop-out windows stay BETA while they are fixed)
Browser: copy your backup to the clipboard, and a small "works offline, your data is local" sign

Desktop: better automatic backups into the folder you choose (today's backup stays up to date and every backup is checked), and a crash log with an option to send details (nothing is ever sent automatically)

items.text: Desktop: pop-out windows fit their size properly when you reopen them (Mac)
Desktop: if Research is popped out, Continue with Clipy opens Clipy's own pop-out

upcoming.title: Find things faster
items: Search shortcuts: tag:, folder:, course:, @today, @tomorrow, @week, @overdue, is:open, type:task, in the search and in Find
"What did I do this week?", answered by Clipy (finish times for tasks and assignments are recorded from now on)
A keyboard shortcut list (Ctrl or Cmd and /), recent apps in the Start menu, and a one-key 25-minute timer (T)
Clipy no longer adds events or tasks unless you ask, and a broken request is never shown in the chat
Desktop: Shut Down on the Start menu closes the app
The in-app update notes show the tagline, tags, BETA and date, and only the features for the version you use

upcoming.title: Looks and first impressions
items: Friendlier empty screens that tell you what to do first
Notes that print cleanly
Browser: a short 3-step tour the first time you open it
Desktop: a check of Windows full screen

upcoming.title: Stability update
items: No new features. A full check for bugs, security and speed, and everything found during 1.4.1 to 1.4.4 gets fixed

upcoming.title: The next Major update
items: Browser: a phone-friendly layout for Today, and sharing links into Favorites from a phone
Desktop: a Mac menu bar dropdown with today's schedule and tasks
The rest of the 1.5 cycle's Minor updates will be added here once 1.5 gets closer

released.summary: A stability release: two security fixes in how notes are shown, a safer graphing calculator, web lookups that can't reach your own network, changes in two browser tabs that merge instead of overwriting, quicker start-up, easier-to-read text, and a Jump to row in Control Panel.

Windows and Linux can update by themselves (you choose: automatic, ask first, or just tell me), Windows Now Playing checks every media session, Clipy has an Undo button and can make flash cards, pop-outs remember their size and position, the website shows a new-version bar, and the browser warns when storage is nearly full.

Clipy can add events, reminders, tasks and assignments when you ask (with an optional switch to write them to Apple Calendar), tidier pop-outs and a File > Pop Out App menu, no more back-to-back Clipy tips, and an accurate storage bar in the browser.
Write to Apple Calendar and Reminders (Mac), pop-out windows for apps, Apple's on-device model for M.X.E.S., optional Now Playing cover lookup, and loading your desktop backup in the browser.
Important fix: saved data wasn't read after updating if you had folders or structured citations.
Windows fixes: full screen, tougher saving, an optional taskbar number, a taskbar menu, and troubleshooting buttons.
Command palette, tags and courses, folders as course hubs, shortcuts you can change, and a better update checker.
Citation Maker 2.0, Sketch Pad 2.0, a flash-card hotkey, and Now Playing in the taskbar clock.
Apple Calendar and Reminders (reading), Periodic Table 2.0, and a calendar in the taskbar clock.
